+# Contributing to WLex
+
+Thanks for contributing! This project follows a "tests-first" approach for bug fixes and asks that all code changes be covered by tests.
+
+## Basics
+
+- Be concise and focused in each change (one feature/fix per PR).
+- Use Conventional Commits for commit messages (see `.github/commit-instructions.md`).
+- Run the test suite and ensure all specs pass before opening a PR: `bundle install && bundle exec rake spec`
+
+## Tests
+
+- **All code changes must include tests.** Unit tests belong under `spec/unit` and integration tests under `spec/integration`.
+- **For bug fixes, add a failing test first.** Create an `rspec` example that reproduces the bug, verify it fails, then implement your fix and ensure the test passes.
+- Keep tests small and deterministic — isolate behavior and avoid external network or file-system side effects when possible.
+
+- **When to use RSpec vs Cucumber:**
+  - **RSpec:** Preferred for unit tests that exercise library internals. Place examples under `spec/unit`.
+  - **Cucumber:** Preferred for integration and user-acceptance tests that describe system behavior from a user's perspective. Place feature files under `features/` and keep scenarios fast and deterministic (mock external services if needed).
+  - For bug fixes, prefer adding  a **Cucumber** scenario.
+- **Snapshot testing (when to use):**
+  - Use snapshot tests for complex or richly structured outputs that are cumbersome to assert field-by-field (generated HTML, serialized ASTs, CLI output, or long text fixtures).
+  - Avoid snapshots for small, easily-specified values (use focused assertions) or for outputs that are non-deterministic unless they can be normalized.
+  - Best practices: store snapshots under `spec/snapshots/` or alongside examples (e.g., `spec/.../expected/`), keep snapshots small and well-scoped, review snapshot diffs carefully in PRs, and update snapshots intentionally with a clear commit message.
+### Example template for a bug reproduction (RSpec)
+
+```ruby
+# spec/unit/your_feature_issue_123_spec.rb
+RSpec.describe "issue #123 - short summary" do
+  it "reproduces the buggy behaviour" do
+    # Arrange: set up minimal state
+
+    # Act: call the method that currently fails
+
+    # Assert: expect the current (incorrect) behaviour
+    # For example:
+    # expect(subject.some_method(arg)).to eq(expected_value)
+  end
+end
+```
+
+You may mark the example `pending` if you want to land the test first without failing CI, but the preferred flow is to keep it failing locally, implement the fix, and then see it pass.
+
+## Git hooks
+
+We include an optional local git hook that runs the unit test suite on commit. To install hooks locally run:
+
+```sh
+bin/install-git-hooks
+```
+
+This will copy `.githooks/pre-commit` to your `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and make it executable. The hook runs unit specs (`rake spec:unit`) and will prevent the commit if unit tests fail.
+
+## Reporting bugs
+
+When filing bugs, include a minimal reproduction and, if possible, an RSpec example that reproduces the problem.
+
+---
+
+Thanks for improving WLex — tests make contributions safer and faster to review. ✅
